q: What does WYSIWYG stand for in word processing?
options: What You See Is Where You Go
Why You See It, We Give
What You See Is What You Get
Where You Select Is What You Gain
explain: WYSIWYG means What You See Is What You Get: the editing screen closely matches the final printed page.

q: What was the original name of Microsoft Word?
explain: Word began life as Multi-Tool Word before being renamed Microsoft Word.

q: Microsoft Word was originally developed by which pair of developers?
explain: Charles Simonyi and Richard Brodie are the key developers of Word. Bricklin and Frankston created VisiCalc, a spreadsheet.

q: In which year was Microsoft Word first released?
explain: The first release was in 1983. The Macintosh version followed in 1985 and Word for Windows in 1989.

q: Which version of Microsoft Word introduced the Ribbon user interface?
explain: The Ribbon replaced the older menus and toolbars in Word 2007.

q: Which of the following is NOT a word processor?
explain: Numbers is Apple's spreadsheet application. Writer (LibreOffice), WordPerfect (Corel) and Pages (Apple) are word processors.

q: Which of the following is NOT controlled by the ruler in Word?
explain: The ruler adjusts indents, tab stops and margin boundaries. Font colour is set from the Font group.

q: What is the desktop zoom range of Microsoft Word?
explain: Word zooms from 10% to 500%, with 100% as the normal reference. The 10% - 400% range belongs to Excel.

q: Which file extension identifies a macro-enabled Word document?
explain: .docm is the Open XML macro-enabled document. A plain .docx cannot store VBA macros.

q: An Excel worksheet is embedded inside a Word document using OLE. What is Word's role?
explain: The application that holds the object is the container/client (Word); the application that supplies the object is the source/server (Excel).

q: Which shortcut opens the Macros dialog in Word?
explain: Alt + F8 opens the Macros dialog. Alt + F4 closes the active window.

q: From which Windows 11 version was WordPad removed?
explain: WordPad was removed starting with Windows 11 version 24H2 (and from Windows Server 2025).

q: In newer Microsoft 365 versions of Word, which shortcut pastes text only?
explain: In newer builds Ctrl + Shift + V pastes text only, while Ctrl + Alt + C / Ctrl + Alt + V copy and paste formatting.

q: Which font and size were the common defaults in Word 2007 to Word 2021?
explain: Calibri 11 pt was the usual default from 2007 to 2021. Word 2003 used Times New Roman 12 pt and newer Microsoft 365 uses Aptos.

q: What is the range of font sizes that can be applied in Word?
explain: Word allows 1 to 1,638 pt, including half-point values. The dropdown presets only run from 8 to 72 pt.

q: What does pressing Ctrl + ] do to selected text?
options: Increases the font size by 1 pt
Jumps to the next preset font size
explain: Ctrl + ] and Ctrl + [ change the size by 1 pt. Ctrl + Shift + > and < step through the preset sizes.

q: Which shortcut applies subscript, as needed for H2O?
explain: Ctrl + = gives subscript; Ctrl + Shift + = gives superscript.

q: Applying the 'tOGGLE cASE' option to the word 'Banking' gives which result?
explain: Toggle case reverses the case of every letter, so Banking becomes bANKING.

q: Which shortcut applies the Small Caps font effect?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + K is Small Caps, whereas Ctrl + Shift + A is All Caps.

q: In a justified paragraph, what normally happens to the last line?
options: It is stretched to both margins
explain: Justify (Ctrl + J) aligns most lines to both margins, but the final line usually stays left-aligned.

q: With no existing selection, pressing F8 three times selects which part of the text?
explain: One press activates Extend Selection, two presses select the word and three presses select the sentence. Esc exits the mode.

q: Which shortcut opens the Thesaurus in Word?
explain: Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus. F7 starts the spelling and grammar check, and Shift + F3 changes case.

q: What is the size of Letter paper in inches?
explain: Letter is 8.5 x 11 inches. A4 is 210 x 297 mm (about 8.27 x 11.69 inches).

q: What is the standard default margin setting from Word 2007 onward?
explain: Word 2007 onward uses 1 inch on all sides. Word 2003 and earlier used 1.25 inches on the left and right.

q: What is the 'gutter' in Word's page setup?
options: The gap between header and body text
Extra space at the binding edge
The space between two text columns
explain: The gutter is extra space at the binding edge so that text is not hidden by a book's spine.

q: If '2, 5-8' is typed in the custom print range, how many pages are printed?
explain: It prints page 2 and pages 5, 6, 7 and 8, which makes 5 pages in total.

q: Format Painter belongs to which group on the Home tab?
explain: The Clipboard group holds Cut, Copy, Paste and Format Painter. Format Painter copies formatting, not text.

q: What does a Drop Cap do?
options: Enlarges a paragraph's first letter across several lines
Turns the whole paragraph into capital letters
Lowers selected text below the baseline
Removes all capital letters from a paragraph
explain: Drop Cap, found in the Text group of the Insert tab, enlarges the opening letter across several lines.

q: Which tab contains Watermark, Page Colour and Page Borders?
explain: These form the Page Background group of the Design tab, which controls the document's coordinated appearance.

q: Which Layout command controls how text flows around a picture?
explain: Wrap Text sets text flow around an object. Position only locates the object on the page.

q: In mail merge, the placeholders for variable details such as a recipient's name and address are called what?
explain: Merge fields are placeholders in the main document. The data source holds the recipient records.

q: Which tab contains Table of Contents, Footnotes and Citations & Bibliography?
explain: All three are groups on the References tab, along with Captions, Index and Table of Authorities.

q: Which of the following is NOT a traditional Word view?
explain: Slide Sorter is a PowerPoint view. Word's traditional views are Print Layout, Read Mode, Web Layout, Outline and Draft.

q: Where are document properties commonly found in Word?
explain: Properties is not a universal View command; document properties are commonly under File > Info.

q: On which date did Microsoft announce the closure of the Office.com Clip Art and image library?
explain: The closure was announced on 1 December 2014, and Bing Image Search became the alternative.

q: What is the maximum number of columns a table can have in Word?
explain: A Word table allows 63 columns. The larger figures belong to Excel worksheets, and text-layout columns are a different feature.

q: Which shortcut splits a table, with the cursor placed in the row that should start the new table?
explain: Ctrl + Shift + Enter splits a table. Ctrl + Enter inserts a page break and Shift + Enter a line break.

q: Which of the following is the AI assistant that can help draft, rewrite and summarise text in supported Word subscriptions?
explain: Copilot is the AI helper in supported editions. Cortana was a separate Microsoft digital assistant and has been retired.
